app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is caller-controlled with no maximum and no floor, so a public endpoint accepts `limit=1000000` (unbounded materialization + serialization of every member) or `limit=-1`/`offset=-1` which emits `LIMIT -1`/`OFFSET -1` and 500s.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — `usernames.split(",").each { |u| User.find_by_username(u) }` is a textbook N+1: one query per username on an unbounded, un-deduped, un-capped comma string instead of a single `User.where(username_lower: names)` batch, so one request can issue thousands of round trips.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:72 — usernames that resolve to no user are silently dropped and the endpoint still returns `success_json`, so the client believes all members were added and its optimistic reload shows a different set than requested with no partial-failure signal.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:73 — `group.add(user)` mutations are persisted immediately inside the loop with no surrounding transaction, so the later `if group.save ... else render_json_error` gate misreports: on failure the error response is returned even though earlier adds are already committed.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — `group.users.delete(user_id)` bypasses the domain removal path used everywhere else (adds go through `group.add(user)`), so any GroupUser callbacks, notification/trust-level side effects, and the cached `groups.user_count` derived column are updated on the add path but not the remove path — asymmetric writes leaving the counter permanently drifted.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — removal is unvalidated and unscoped: no check that `user_id` is actually a member, so a delete of a non-member returns 200 success, and the subsequent `group.save` can never fail, making the `render_json_error` branch dead code.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:38 — `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"` is applied unconditionally on every update, so any partial PUT that omits `visible` (now legal since the params moved from a nested `group:` hash to flat top-level keys) silently flips the group to invisible — a destructive default in a full-replace update masquerading as a patch.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:22 — API-CONTRACT-BREAKING: create/update moved from nested `params[:group][...]` to flat top-level params and the `PATCH` `changes[:add]/[:delete]` membership API was deleted outright, so existing scripted admin clients now either 500 on `params.require` or write nothing while returning 200.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:21 — SENTINEL-MEANING-CHANGE: `findMembers` now returns bare `undefined` for an unnamed group where it previously returned `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`, and on success it resolves to `undefined` instead of the member array, so any caller still doing `.then(function(members){...})` (routes, plugins) gets a TypeError or silently receives nothing.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:47 — the reload `self.findMembers()` inside `removeMember`/`addMembers` is neither returned nor error-handled, so the outer promise resolves before the list is refreshed and a failed reload leaves the UI showing stale membership with no error surfaced.

app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — `totalPages = Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` is off by one on exact multiples (50 members / limit 50 reports 2 pages), so `showingLast` stays false and "next" navigates to a guaranteed-empty page.

app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:23 — offset is clamped with `Math.min(user_count, offset)` rather than to a page boundary, so after removing the last member of a page (user_count shrinks) the client requests `offset == total` and renders an empty member list with `currentPage > totalPages` and no way to recover except reload.

app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:25 — `total = group.users.count` runs a fresh COUNT on every page request and becomes a second source of truth for member count alongside the cached `user_count` column that `BasicGroupSerializer` exposes and the client also stores, so the two can disagree in the same UI.

app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:73 — `group.add(user)` is called with no check that the user is already a member and no spec for the duplicate-add case, so re-submitting the same username list can create duplicate group_users rows or blow up on the unique index (500) instead of being a no-op.
